This is a **regression**, see my [comment](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/19934#issuecomment-339661814) below.

~~Actually `routerLinkActive` is working fine here~~, try replace:

```html
<a ... routerLinkActive #rla="routerLinkActive" [class.active]="rla.isActive">
```

to:

```html
<a ... routerLinkActive="active">
```

Then you'll find it update as expected.

The problem here is, `[class.active]="rla.isActive"` is your component's own binding, not `routerLinkActive`'s, so even `rla.isActive` is updated successfully, the `class.active` of your component won't be updated (in `OnPush`).

---

You can instead make a feature request like:

**`RouterLinkActive` should perform change detection whenever status of `isActive` changes.**

<sub>Likely too tricky for an attribute directive to control `ChangeDetector` in background.</sub>

Or

**`RouterLinkActive` should expose an Observable version of `isActive` (on status change) so that component can use `async` pipe on it (without change detection on each tick).**

I have a problem that I think is some kind of race condition..? ```html {{ category.name }}

test

 ``` I would expect the rla.isActive to be true for 1 item. the `routerLinkActive="'active'"` does work fine and the element does get class="active" Any ideas?

It's just the nature of Angular's change detection mechanism. It would only update the view after dirty-checking the bound value.

So since your own component is behind `OnPush`, although `rla.isActive` is changed, but your component won't check its result, then no update is applied to the view of your component.
I see.. do you have any pointers on how I could work around this until we can upgrade to angular5 where it has been solved :)

Some update, this is likely to be a **regression**, it should work before the https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/82417b3ca59aa2e5f41ee12db4cb18970b5b4f47 change (which is a fix of another regression).

In which the `ChangeDetectorRef#detectChanges()` call has been removed.

Could you please update the issue body to reflect it?
I think "RouterLinkActive should expose an Observable version of isActive" is a great idea. Any chance it will be implemented?
@vicb Can you take a look at this? It appears we regressed with your change #15943.
Any updates on this? The suggested workaround is somehow not working for me despite the class being set.
